REWRITE: a node keeps its identity and changes its content
PARTITION: a state node is replaced by the k irreducible components of a symmetry representation (R1)
EXTEND: each irreducible block becomes a Fock ladder (R3)
SPLIT: a sector splits in two after an observable distinguishes them (R8)
REPLACE: k sectors are replaced by k others after an observable shows compositeness (R8)
MERGE: k model nodes that share a calibration become one (R6)
ABSORB: an effective node becomes the low-energy limit of a fundamental one (R7)
CLUSTER: fundamental nodes grouped by Lagrangian term (R10)
LINEAGE: an absorption trace recorded inside a cluster
ROUTE: legs = (sector, n) pairs of the fields of a term (R4)
PREDICT: a model node reaches an observable (status pred)
FLAG: an observable has in-degree 0 from the model layer (R2 precondition)
SIGNAL: two model nodes share a calibration edge (R6 precondition)
BACK: a model node acts on the state layer
DERIVE: a reading-indexed route combines model and state nodes (readers)
FAIL: a prediction route fails; a later route to the same target resolves it
COMPOSE: a new independent sector is adjoined by tensor product (Rule II of the inference engine)
REDUCE: parameters tied by symmetry, representation reduced by the commutant (Rule III of the inference engine)
CONTRACT: a fixed model node is suppressed: an H-graph becomes an E-graph (Prop. contraction)
CENSUS: enumerate the cells (pairs) of a layer pair with no recorded edge
CLOSE: settle a cell by composition, elementary proof, counterexample or literature fill

rules.11: reading-order growth (readers): a node appears at the paragraph that introduces it, a route at the paragraph that explains it; no forward links
rules.12: failed-route resolution (readers): a failed route is followed by a successful route into the same target
rules.13: census (effect/resource branches): every pair of a designated layer pair without an edge is a candidate
rules.14: closure (effect/resource branches): a candidate is settled by composition, elementary proof, counterexample or literature fill
rules.15: compose (inference engine): adjoin an independent sector by tensor product when refit fails
rules.16: reduce (inference engine): tie parameters when the evidence favours it and decompose by the commutant
